concepts.def: Central Processing Unit: executes instructions from memory using the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
Arithmetic Logic Unit: performs arithmetic and logical operations within the CPU.
CPU component that directs operations by interpreting instructions and sending control signals.
Small, very fast storage location inside the CPU (e.g., PC, MAR, MDR, accumulator).

Small high-speed memory between CPU and RAM that stores frequently used data.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hardware — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Hardware brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Hardware.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
